I'm an ecosystem ecologist and biogeochemist. I study how carbon, nutrients, and greenhouse gases move through ecosystems, and what that means for Earth's climate, soils, and water. Ecosystems and climate shape each other: warming, drought, storms, pathogens, and land use alter how ecosystems function, which in turn affects whether they capture or release climate-warming gases. I study both directions of that relationship.

Plants and microbes drive these cycles, so that's where I focus: which species and communities are present, how they interact, and how their activity adds up, from the microbes living inside a single tree to whole forests and wetlands. I use field measurements, experiments, molecular tools, and sensors I help build. I'm also interested in how this understanding can inform land and nutrient management, greenhouse gas accounting, natural carbon capture, and climate engineering.

I'm a [Stanford Science Fellow](https://stanfordsciencefellows.stanford.edu/) in the [Department of Earth System Science](https://earthsystemscience.stanford.edu/), working with the [Jackson Lab](https://jacksonlab.stanford.edu/). I completed my PhD at the [Yale School of the Environment](https://environment.yale.edu/) in 2026, and have been a research fellow at [Harvard Forest](https://harvardforest.fas.harvard.edu/), an LTER Synthesis Fellow with [NCEAS](https://nceas.ucsb.edu/), and adjunct faculty in the [Connecticut College Department of Botany](https://www.conncoll.edu/academics/majors-departments-programs/departments/botany/).
